chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from 'Ammar al-Sabati said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a boy who was breastfed by a woman: is it permissible for him to marry her sister by the father through breastfeeding? He said, so he said, 'No, for they have all breastfed from the milk of one male (sire) from one woman.'

I said: Does he marry her sister by the mother through breastfeeding? He said, 'There is no harm with that, for her sister who did not breastfeed him, her sire was different from the sire of the one who breastfed the boy, so the two sires differed, so there is no harm.'

key_terms.أُخْتَهَا لِأَبِيهَا: Her sister by the father (paternal half-sister)
key_terms.أُخْتَهَا لِأُمِّهَا: Her sister by the mother (maternal half-sister)
key_terms.فَحْل: Sire/Male (used here to denote the father's lineage affecting the milk)

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his wet nurse's half-sister if they have different fathers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia juristic principle that the prohibition of *radāʿ* (breastfeeding) is contingent upon the milk originating from the same male lineage (*fahl*), rather than merely the female nurse. It distinguishes between full sisters, who share the same paternal milk source and thus remain prohibited, and half-sisters with different fathers, whose distinct milk lineages permit marriage. This nuance highlights the Shia emphasis on the biological and genealogical specifics of milk kinship in determining marital validity.
